<!--
Source: Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman (2009), ESL 2e, section 7.10.1,
which computes standard-error bars for the CV curve from the K per-fold
errors and states the one-standard-error rule.
-->
:::{#def-cv-se}
#### Standard error of a cross-validation estimate

Let $\operatorname{MSE}_1, \ldots, \operatorname{MSE}_k$
be the [mean squared errors](estimation.qmd#def-prediction-mse)
of the predictions for the observations in folds $1, \ldots, k$
of [$k$-fold cross-validation](#def-kfold),
and let $s_{\text{CV}}$ be their
[sample standard deviation](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample-sd).
The **standard error** of the cross-validation estimate is

$$
\operatorname{SE}_{\text{CV}} \eqdef \frac{s_{\text{CV}}}{\sqrt{k}}.
$$ {#eq-cv-se}

:::
